column1: # Seed brands for public.parse_item (German groceries and drugstore). Format, tab-separated:
# brand: the display name, as the brand writes itself (elmex, Ja!, Coca-Cola). The parser matches
#   it ignoring case, umlauts, spaces, dots, hyphens and apostrophes (public.brand_key), so list
#   one spelling: Coca-Cola also matches "Coca Cola", Dr. Oetker "Dr Oetker", Beck's "Becks".
# product (optional): the item a text that is only the brand means: "Pampers" is Windeln with
#   the brand Pampers. Only for brands people say instead of the product. Without one, a text
#   that is only the brand keeps it as its name ("Nutella"). With one, a single name word of
#   another kind (food, drinks, non-food) or one the dictionary does not know is the variety:
#   "Whiskas Lachs" is Katzenfutter, Whiskas, Lachs. So a brand whose range spans kinds gets no
#   product (Purina, Royal Canin, Vitakraft: cat and dog; Lipton, Teekanne: Tee and Eistee).
# store (optional): dm, lidl or edeka, only for that store's own brands. The parser tags the
#   item with the household's store of that seed key.
# Left out on purpose, because the word is an ordinary word, an Eigenschaft or voice filler
#   Kinder (Ferrero; "Zahnpasta Kinder" is a property), Danke (toilet paper; "danke" ends many
#   dictated sentences), Ja (without "!"), Bio, Extra (chewing gum), Absolut (vodka), Klar,
#   Rauch, Wolf, Fuchs, Ruf, Lift, Hugo, Gourmet, Corona, Ritter (alone; Ritter Sport is in),
#   Müller (also a drugstore chain a household may add as a store), Appel (fish; reads as a
#   typo of Apfel), Harry (bread; a first name), 3 Glocken (starts with an amount, so the
